_comment: copy to bench_config.json and edit. Anything null/empty degrades gracefully: no chirpstack -> WARN instead of server assertions; no gateway cmds -> interactive prompts (stage-c refuses to run unattended without them).
_factor: 1.0 = real time. Smaller scales the SHORT timeouts only (harness debugging, never for results). stage-c always real time.

gateway._comment: How the harness takes the node's network path down/up. type: 'tasmota' (mains switch on the LAN powering the GATEWAY ONLY — server must stay up; set ip and optional password), 'shell' (off_cmd/on_cmd, e.g. ssh stop/start of the packet forwarder or chirpstack-gateway-bridge), 'manual' (interactive prompt; fine for stages A/B, stage-c refuses unattended). A failed tasmota call or missing switch is FATAL, never silently ignored. on_wait_s: after ON, wait for the gateway to boot (default 90 s for tasmota, 0 for shell) so recovery times compare fairly.

chirpstack._comment: ChirpStack v4 internal REST API (login session: gives lastSeenAt + FCntUp). ONLY for ChirpStack v4 deployments — v3 has no usable REST API, use the mqtt block there. null/empty = the mqtt/db probes are used instead (serial-only pass/fail if neither exists).

mqtt._comment: ChirpStack MQTT integration (broker that the ChirpStack v3/v4 service publishes to). Preferred server probe for v3: subscribe-only, topic application/+/device/<dev_eui>/event/up, gives arrival time + exact fCnt (B1.5 continuity). Requires paho-mqtt (pip install paho-mqtt). null host = probe off.
